controller.Address: Str. X nr. 0, Town X, Romania
controller.Data Protection Officer (DPO): Not appointed. The assessment of 1 December 2026 concluded that appointment is not mandatory because the practice does not carry out large-scale processing (recital 91 GDPR). Reviewed yearly.
controller.Joint controllers: None. The visiting physician (Dr. B) is treated as a separate controller for the records of his own patients; the arrangement is to be confirmed.

activities.title: Appointments
activities.purpose: Scheduling patients for consultations and investigations and managing the clinic diary.
activities.subjects: Patients; legal representatives or carers who make the appointment.
activities.data: Name, phone, e-mail; date and time of the appointment; family or internal medicine consultation, ECG, ultrasound, blood sampling; reason for the appointment, only as far as necessary (it may reveal health information).
activities.basis: Art. 6(1)(b) – steps taken at the patient's request before entering into the medical services contract, and its performance.
activities.art9: Art. 9(2)(h), where the reason for the appointment contains health data.
activities.source: The data subject (phone, e-mail, contact form on the website, see PA-13, in person at reception).
activities.recipients: Medical and reception staff; the Practice Software Provider (V-01) and the E-mail Provider (V-06) – processors.
activities.transfers: No. Hosting is in the EU; the e-mail provider's support access is checked in the vendor review.
activities.retention: See RET-07 in the retention schedule.
activities.security: Individual accounts; the diary is not visible to patients; no diagnoses are written in the diary; reception screen positioned away from the waiting room.
activities.assessments: No separate assessment needed. The website contact form is covered in PA-13.

activities.title: Providing medical services and keeping medical records
activities.purpose: Consultations, diagnosis, treatment, prescriptions, medical recommendations and referrals; creating and keeping the medical record and the registers required by law.
activities.data: Identification data (name, national ID number, ID document); contact data; medical history, diagnosis, treatments, tests, prescriptions, recommendations; health insurance data.
activities.basis: Art. 6(1)(b) – the medical services contract; (c) – legal obligations (medical records). National ID number: Art. 4 of Law no. 190/2018.
activities.art9: Art. 9(2)(h), in compliance with Art. 9(3) (professional secrecy).
activities.source: The patient; other doctors or healthcare providers (referrals, results); the health insurance fund – checking insured status.
activities.recipients: Doctors and medical staff involved in care; medical collaborators when needed; the Practice Software Provider (V-01) and the IT Support Provider (V-03; remote support, no routine access to records) – processors; authorities, on a lawful request.
activities.transfers: No. Hosting is in the EU (see V-01).
activities.security: Role-based access, only for staff involved in care; individual accounts; access log kept by the practice software and checked during the periodic access review; paper files in locked rooms; backups; staff confidentiality undertaking.
activities.assessments: DPIA threshold assessment: December 2026 (see module 12). Processing by a small practice is in principle not "large scale" (recital 91 GDPR); documented in the threshold assessment.

activities.title: Reporting to the health insurance fund and other authorities
activities.purpose: Meeting legal obligations for reporting, claims and inspections by the health insurance fund and other competent authorities.
activities.data: Identification data including the national ID number; data on services provided; diagnosis, as far as the reporting requires.
activities.basis: Art. 6(1)(c) – legal obligations. National ID number: Art. 4 of Law no. 190/2018.
activities.art9: Art. 9(2)(h). To be confirmed for specific reports; a public-interest condition such as (i) may fit better.
activities.recipients: The county health insurance fund and other competent authorities, through their IT platforms.
activities.security: Transmission only through the official platforms; individual user accounts; the digital certificate is held by Dr. A.

activities.title: Invoicing and accounting
activities.purpose: Issuing invoices and receipts, collecting payments, accounting and tax records.
activities.subjects: Patients, or the person who pays for the services.
activities.data: Name, address; national ID number only where an insurance claim or the law requires it; name of the service (minimum description); amount; method of payment; health insurance data where applicable.
activities.basis: Art. 6(1)(c) – accounting and tax law; (b) – the services contract.
activities.art9: Art. 9(2)(h), where the description of a service reveals health data; descriptions are kept to the minimum necessary.
activities.recipients: The Accounting Firm (V-04) – processor; tax authorities; the Card Payment Provider (V-11) – separate controller; the Shredding Provider (V-10) – processor.
activities.security: Accounting documents in locked files; sent to the accountant through an encrypted channel agreed with the Accounting Firm; limited access.

activities.title: Laboratories and other healthcare providers (referrals and results)
activities.purpose: Sending and receiving referrals, test and investigation results and medical letters, to ensure continuity of care.
activities.data: Identification data; relevant medical data (tests, imaging, diagnosis).
activities.source: The patient; the medical record; laboratories and other providers.
activities.recipients: The Partner Laboratory (V-08) and the specialists to whom the patient is referred – separate controllers.
activities.transfers: No. Providers are in the EU.
activities.security: Transmission through secure channels (results are received on the clinic business e-mail and filed in the patient record); medical data is not sent through personal messaging apps.

activities.title: Communications about appointments and treatment
activities.purpose: Appointment reminders and confirmations; information about treatment recommendations or available results (service messages, not marketing).
activities.data: Name, phone or e-mail, date and time of the appointment; minimal medical information.
activities.art9: Art. 9(2)(h), where a message could reveal health data; messages are written without diagnosis or medical details.
activities.security: Message templates without medical data; checking the phone number / e-mail address; sender name shows the clinic only, not a medical specialty.
activities.assessments: None needed while the provider stays in the EU.

activities.title: Video surveillance (CCTV)
activities.purpose: Safety of patients and staff, protection of property, prevention and investigation of security incidents.
activities.subjects: Patients, visitors, staff, couriers and suppliers.
activities.data: Video images from common areas; date and time. The system does not record sound.
activities.art9: The clinic does not aim to process special-category data. The medical context could allow inferences about health, so cameras are limited to common areas and access to images is restricted.
activities.recipients: Authorised staff (Dr. A only); authorities, on a lawful request; the CCTV Installer (V-05) – processor, only if it has access to recordings, under supervision.
activities.transfers: No. Recordings stay on the local recorder.
activities.retention: See RET-06 (7 days; never more than 30).
activities.security: Access with an individual account and password; automatic deletion by overwriting; recorder in a locked cabinet; log of video exports; signage at the entrance; no cameras in consultation rooms, the treatment room, toilets or the staff room.
activities.assessments: Legitimate interest assessment (LIA) – module 10, completed December 2026. DPIA threshold check: December 2026. For employees: Art. 5 of Law no. 190/2018 (well-founded legitimate interest, prior information, consultation of the union or employee representatives, necessity of the measure, storage of no more than 30 days, with the exceptions in law).

activities.title: Promotional communications
activities.purpose: Information about new services and clinic campaigns, only with the person's consent.
activities.data: Name, e-mail address or phone; proof of consent (date and method).
activities.art9: No health data is processed for promotion (the contact list is not segmented by diagnosis or treatment).
activities.security: List kept separate from the medical records; unsubscribe option in every message; withdrawal of consent is processed immediately.
activities.assessments: Check compliance with the rules on unsolicited commercial communications (Law no. 506/2004 – to be verified).

activities.title: Handling data subject requests
activities.purpose: Receiving, assessing and answering requests to exercise rights under the GDPR, and keeping proof of the reply.
activities.subjects: Patients, employees and others who make requests; their representatives.
activities.data: Identification data; content of the request; proof of identity; correspondence and the reply.
activities.basis: Art. 6(1)(c) – the legal obligation in Art. 12–22 GDPR.
activities.art9: Where the request contains health data: Art. 9(2)(f) or (h) – to be confirmed.
activities.recipients: Authorised staff; the external privacy adviser, if needed.
activities.security: Register kept separate from the medical record; identity checked before data is released; limited access.

activities.title: Handling personal data breaches
activities.purpose: Documenting every personal data breach (Art. 33(5) GDPR), notifying the supervisory authority and informing affected people when required.
activities.subjects: People affected by a breach (patients, staff).
activities.data: Description of the breach; categories and approximate number of people and records; consequences; measures taken; contact details.
activities.basis: Art. 6(1)(c) – the obligations in Art. 33 and 34 GDPR.
activities.art9: The register does not contain the medical data of affected people, only categories and numbers.
activities.recipients: The supervisory authority; affected people; the IT Support Provider (V-03) and the external privacy adviser, if involved.
activities.security: Register with limited access; breaches are reported internally without delay.

activities.title: HR and payroll
activities.purpose: Concluding and running employment or collaboration contracts, payroll, tax and social obligations, working time records, health and safety at work, occupational health.
activities.data: Identification data including the national ID number; contact; education and qualifications; licence to practise and professional authorisations; contract; salary and bank account; attendance and leave; occupational health certificate.
activities.art9: Art. 9(2)(b) – obligations in employment and social security law (for example sick leave, occupational health certificate).
activities.source: The data subject; authorities; the occupational health provider.
activities.recipients: The Accounting Firm (V-04) – processor for payroll; labour, tax and social security authorities; the Occupational Health Provider (V-12) – separate controller; the professional college; the employee's bank.
activities.security: Personnel files locked; access limited to management and Dr. A.

activities.title: Recruitment
activities.data: CV, contact details, education and experience, other information the candidate sends.
activities.basis: Art. 6(1)(b) – steps taken at the candidate's request; (a) – consent, to keep the CV for future positions.
activities.recipients: Staff designated for recruitment, in practice Dr. A.
activities.security: Limited access; CVs are not circulated through insecure channels.

activities.title: Website and cookies
activities.purpose: Operation and security of the website, informing the public, contact form.
activities.data: IP address; strictly necessary cookies; analytics cookies, with consent; data entered in the form.
activities.basis: Art. 6(1)(f) – website security and strictly necessary cookies; (a) – consent for non-essential cookies (Law no. 506/2004 – to be verified).
activities.art9: The form does not ask for health data. Visitors are asked not to write medical details in the form.
activities.recipients: The Hosting Provider (V-07) – processor; the analytics tool provider, to be confirmed in the vendor review.
activities.transfers: No by design; to be confirmed for the analytics tool.
activities.security: HTTPS; regular updates; cookie banner; administrator access with strong authentication.
activities.assessments: Cookie policy – published on the website with the cookie banner.
